er_v06_c21_b001_01: Today I'm really here to buy something.
er_v06_c21_b001_02: You sold something last time too.
er_v06_c21_b001_03: Last time I also said a lot of things I shouldn't have said for her.
er_v06_c21_b001_05: I did. She said don't just apologise to the owner, as if she doesn't have a mouth of her own.
er_v06_c21_b001_06: I saw her mother. Thinner than before. Still talks the same way, won't let anyone praise her too much.
er_v06_c21_b001_08: Eleanor told me about recent events too. This time, I heard the whole story from beginning to end.
er_v06_c21_b002_01: That bracelet. I had someone look at it when I got back. Your price was fairer than mine.
er_v06_c21_b002_02: When I tell people about it, they don't believe there's a shopkeeper like that in the lower levels.
er_v06_c21_b003_01: Before, when we picked gifts, we only worried they weren't expensive enough.
er_v06_c21_b003_02: This time she told me to bring things that are actually useful, not turn a visit into an exhibition.
er_v06_c21_b003_04: She is. It's the tone that makes it hard to admit right away.
er_v06_c21_b004_02: Do you have any conditions to raise?
er_v06_c21_b004_03: No. It's just that when she said it, she had no intention of asking my opinion.
er_v06_c21_b004_04: Word going around up there is that Eleanor has taken a liking to a pawnshop owner in the lower levels.
er_v06_c21_b004_06: I defended her a little. ...Don't thank me. I did it for her, not you.
er_v06_c21_b005_01: She says you're a friend worth keeping. She rarely uses the word 'worth.'
er_v06_c21_b005_03: I'm learning to understand that again.
er_v06_c21_b006_01: If suitable business comes up in the future, I'll have people come talk to you directly. You won't owe me a favour.
er_v06_c21_b006_02: If the goods are right and the price is right, we'll talk.
er_v06_c21_b006_03: No wonder she says that all the time now.
er_v06_c22_b001_01: My mother found a place willing to let her help organise equipment. Not her old farm, but she wants to go.
er_v06_c22_b001_03: I'll help for a few days. I found steadier work myself too, so I won't have to rely only on scavenging.
er_v06_c22_b001_04: It's not the life we had before, but it's our own.
er_v06_c22_b001_05: I used to think this kind of work didn't count. Now I think being able to support a family on your own is already impressive.
er_v06_c22_b002_01: Someone from the research side came to ask if we'd help organise the records my mother left behind.
er_v06_c22_b002_03: Some of the work is up there. It needs a separate work permit. It's not a return to our old life, and the case isn't closed.
er_v06_c22_b002_04: My mother wants to keep doing research. I want to understand the parts I couldn't follow.
er_v06_c22_b003_01: If you want to go, go.
er_v06_c22_b003_02: Of course I'm going. I didn't come here today to ask for your permission.
er_v06_c22_b003_03: Then you came to notify me?
er_v06_c22_b003_04: I came to discuss how to arrange the time! Can't you let me finish a sentence?
er_v06_c22_b004_01: I want to keep working, and I want to keep seeing you.
er_v06_c22_b004_02: You don't have to turn down an opportunity for this shop.
er_v06_c22_b004_03: I wasn't planning to turn it down. I wasn't planning to turn you down either.
er_v06_c22_b004_04: Before, other people arranged my life for me. All I had to do was pick what I didn't like.
er_v06_c22_b004_05: Now I choose for myself. Don't start deciding 'what's good for me' again.
er_v06_c22_b004_06: Then we'll go with your arrangement. Tell me when you're busy.
er_v06_c22_b004_07: You too. Stop saying the shop can't spare you and skipping proper meals.
er_v06_c22_b005_01: I've thought about what happened last time. I want you to come here as more than a regular.
er_v06_c22_b005_02: Are you sure? You're not going to make me guess again?
er_v06_c22_b005_04: ...All right. I'll make time. You have to make time too.
er_v06_c22_b006_01: I might not come as often in the future. But we can still help each other with business.
er_v06_c22_b006_02: If I come across something suitable, I'll keep an eye out for you.
er_v06_c22_b006_03: Thank you. If you need anything, don't forget to ask me.
er_v06_c22_b007_02: That time you asked for a price and didn't sell it.
er_v06_c22_b007_03: I told my mother I wanted to give it to you. She said it's mine, so I decide.
er_v06_c22_b007_04: And this time it's not for sale?
er_v06_c22_b007_05: No. You'd better have learned to tell the difference by now.
er_v06_c22_b008_02: Don't put it with the goods on the counter. I'm not that generous.
er_v06_c22_b009_01: It looks better on you. I'll take the thought.
er_v06_c22_b009_02: ...Fine. I'll wear it myself. It's not as if you won't see me again.
er_v06_c22_b010_01: I originally wanted to give you that locket. In the end, I sold it to make up the money.
er_v06_c22_b010_02: You don't need to find something else to replace it.
er_v06_c22_b010_03: I know. I just wanted you to know that I thought about it.
er_v06_c23_b001_01: Hey. Do you have time today?
er_v06_c23_b001_03: No. My mother's fine, and I haven't lost my job.
er_v06_c23_b001_04: You'll have to get used to it. Me coming here doesn't always mean something happened.
er_v06_c23_b001_06: Then get used to it faster.
er_v06_c23_b002_01: My mother keeps telling me to bring an extra portion of food.
er_v06_c23_b002_03: She has hers too. This one's for you.
er_v06_c23_b002_04: How are you two doing now?
er_v06_c23_b002_05: The room's still small, and we still have to count every credit. My mother has nightmares sometimes.
er_v06_c23_b002_06: But when she wakes up, I'm right there, and I can answer her.
er_v06_c23_b002_08: Yeah. Not everything has come back. But we're not left with only what we lost.
er_v06_c23_b003_01: The first time I came here, I said your shop wasn't much.
er_v06_c23_b003_03: There's still plenty that needs fixing. Don't think that because I like you, I'll like that broken lamp too.
er_v06_c23_b003_05: You agreed to this. My temper isn't going to vanish just because we're together.
er_v06_c23_b003_07: Then let me stay here with you for a while today. If a customer comes, do your business.
er_v06_c23_b003_11: Anything. Just don't start with 'how much money are you short?'
er_v06_c23_b004_01: I used to think that once I went back up, I wouldn't need to keep in touch with people I met down here.
er_v06_c23_b004_03: Now I know that sorting people by where they live is incredibly stupid.
er_v06_c23_b004_05: You can remember it. Just don't recite it every time you see me.
er_v06_c23_b004_06: Come find me when you need something. Or when you don't. Friends don't only count when someone's short of money.
